experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic achievement.

experiences.name: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, fresh pasta, and local Frascati wine at family-run trattorias and street food stalls. This bohemian neighborhood offers the most authentic Roman culinary experience away from tourist traps.

experiences.name: Borghese Gallery Art Tour
experiences.description: Visit this intimate yet world-class gallery housing Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings inside a baroque villa. Reservations are mandatory and entry is limited to 360 visitors at a time, ensuring an unhurried, immersive experience with masterpieces like Apollo and Daphne.

experiences.name: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Rome's culinary soul at the Mercato Testaccio, the city's most authentic covered food market. Sample porchetta sandwiches, aged pecorino romano, cured meats, and the famously divisive quinto quarto (offal dishes) that define true Roman cucina povera tradition.

experiences.name: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire across the Forum and Palatine Hill, where emperors once lived. Combined with Colosseum entry, this archaeological complex offers unparalleled insight into Roman history and culture, with panoramic views over ruins that inspired Renaissance artists for centuries.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic achievement.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 16:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome, GA airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport, and check in to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome at 15 Chateau Drive. Freshen up and get oriented in the local area around the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll around the Chateau Drive neighborhood to get your bearings. Visit a nearby grocery store (Walmart or Kroger) to stock up on snacks, breakfast items, and drinks to save money throughout the trip — a key budget travel hack.

meals.breakfast: Eaten before or during travel — grab something at the airport.
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or airport snack during travel.
meals.dinner: Zaxby's or Chick-fil-A near the hotel on Shorter Ave — quick, affordable, and filling after a long travel day. Budget ~$10–12 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and recovery. Rome, GA is a small city — not Rome, Italy. Note that the hotel address (15 Chateau Drive, Rome, US 34.2212, -85.1513) places you in Rome, Georgia, USA. Plan local activities accordingly. Keep receipts for all expenses to track your budget.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Rome Area History Museum (open 9 AM) on Broad Street downtown — free or low-cost admission. Explore exhibits on the history of Rome, GA and the surrounding Floyd County area. Afterward, walk along the scenic Oostanaula and Etowah River confluence area near downtown.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore downtown Rome's public art scene — the city has numerous murals, sculptures, and the famous Romulus and Remus Wolf Statue (a gift from Benito Mussolini in 1929, a nod to the city's Italian namesake). Walk the Historic District along Broad Street, window-shopping and admiring the architecture. Visit the free Clock Tower atop Neely Hill for panoramic views of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the cool of the evening (expect highs near 30°C, so evenings are more comfortable) with a walk along the Riverwalk trail along the Coosa River. Watch the sunset from the riverbank.

meals.breakfast: Use groceries purchased last night — cereal, fruit, or yogurt in the hotel room. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Harvest Moon Café on Broad Street — a local favorite with affordable sandwiches and salads. Budget ~$10–13.
meals.dinner: El Sombrero Mexican Restaurant on Turner McCall Blvd — generous portions at budget-friendly prices. Tacos and enchiladas ~$10–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing — June temperatures average 29.8°C. Carry a reusable water bottle. Downtown Rome is very walkable from the hotel via a short drive or rideshare (~5–10 min).

day_by_day.morning: Head to Myrtle Hill Cemetery (free, open daily) — a stunning hilltop cemetery with sweeping views of Rome and the rivers below. It's a surprisingly beautiful and peaceful art-meets-history experience, with ornate Victorian-era monuments and sculptures. Open early, ideal before the heat peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chieftains Museum / Major Ridge Home (National Historic Landmark) — a preserved 1794 log cabin and plantation home with exhibits on Cherokee history and culture. Admission is low-cost (~$5–8). Afterward, browse the Rome Farmers Market (Fridays) for local produce, handmade goods, and affordable snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a live music event or art show at a local venue — check the Rome City Auditorium or local Facebook event pages for free or low-cost Friday night events. Rome has an active arts community.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast with groceries. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab fresh produce and a snack from the Farmers Market — local bread, fruit, and cheese make a perfect picnic lunch by the river. Budget ~$8–10.
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli on Broad Street — a Rome institution with hearty sandwiches and German-inspired comfort food at reasonable prices. Budget ~$12–15.

day_by_day.notes: The Chieftains Museum connects beautifully to art and history interests. Bring cash for the Farmers Market — many vendors are cash-only. Rain chance exists (~33mm monthly average), so carry a compact umbrella.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Coosa Valley Art Center or explore the Berry College campus (free and open to the public) — one of the largest college campuses in the world by acreage, with stunning Gothic architecture, a working farm, and abundant wildlife including deer. The architecture and grounds are genuinely impressive and completely free to walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Shorter University Art Gallery or check local listings for any weekend art exhibitions or open studio events in Rome. Rome has a growing arts scene with several galleries. Alternatively, explore the public sculpture trail along the Riverwalk.
day_by_day.evening: Saturday night in downtown Rome — explore the bar and restaurant scene on Broad Street. Many venues have live music on Saturday evenings at no cover charge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on the Berry College campus grounds — use groceries from your stock. Budget ~$3–5.
meals.dinner: Harvest Moon Café or try Broad Street Brewing Company for affordable pub food and local craft beer in a lively Saturday atmosphere. Budget ~$13–16.

day_by_day.notes: Berry College is about 10–15 minutes from the hotel by car. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the campus is vast. Saturday is the best day to find local art events and community gatherings.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Sunday morning — sleep in, enjoy a hotel room breakfast, then visit the Rome-Floyd County Library which occasionally hosts free art exhibitions and cultural events. Check their calendar in advance. Alternatively, attend a Sunday morning service at one of Rome's historic churches for a free cultural and architectural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or rideshare to Cave Spring, GA (~20 minutes from Rome) — a charming small town with a natural limestone cave (Rolater Park Cave, very low admission ~$2–3), a natural spring, and a beautiful public park with a swimming pool. The cave is a unique geological art-of-nature experience and a great way to cool off from the heat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for a quiet Sunday evening. Cook a simple meal using hotel room amenities or groceries, or opt for an affordable takeout option.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Picnic at Rolater Park in Cave Spring — bring sandwiches and snacks from your grocery stock. Budget ~$3–5.
meals.dinner: Takeout from Zaxby's, Moe's Southwest Grill, or another affordable chain near the hotel. Budget ~$10–12. Or cook ramen/pasta in the hotel room to save maximum budget.

day_by_day.notes: Cave Spring is a hidden gem and very budget-friendly. The cave stays cool (~15°C inside) — a welcome relief from summer heat. Bring a light jacket for the cave tour. Sunday hours may vary for some attractions — call ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Coosa Valley Art Center on East 2nd Avenue — Rome's primary dedicated art space with rotating exhibitions, local artist showcases, and sometimes free or low-cost admission. This directly aligns with your art interest and supports the local creative community.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided food tour of Rome's downtown culinary scene — sample local flavors by visiting 2–3 spots for small bites or drinks. Rome has a surprisingly diverse food scene for a small city. Try a local bakery, a specialty coffee shop, and a local deli or food truck.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset hike or walk at Lock and Dam Park along the Coosa River — a peaceful green space with river views, picnic areas, and walking trails. Free admission. Ideal in the cooler evening hours.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Self-guided food tour — budget ~$15–18 total across multiple small stops. Try Breve Coffee + Kitchen for a light lunch and great coffee.
meals.dinner: Pastime Restaurant on Broad Street — a Rome classic, known for affordable home-style Southern cooking. Meat-and-three style meals ~$10–13.

day_by_day.notes: Monday can be slower for some attractions — call the Coosa Valley Art Center to confirm hours. The food tour approach is a great budget strategy: small portions at multiple places gives variety without overspending. Stay hydrated in the heat.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — revisit your favorite spot from the week for a nostalgic last look. Consider a peaceful walk along the Riverwalk or back up to the Clock Tower for a final panoramic view of the city. Pick up any local souvenirs from downtown shops — look for handmade or locally produced items to support local artists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of La Quinta (standard checkout 11 AM — confirm with hotel). If your departure allows, spend remaining time exploring any missed spots or doing last-minute souvenir shopping on Broad Street. Store luggage at the hotel lobby if needed while you explore.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Rome, GA. Head to the airport or onward destination. Reflect on a successful budget trip — art, food, history, and nature all explored without breaking the bank.

meals.breakfast: Use up remaining grocery items for a final hotel room breakfast. Budget ~$2–3.
meals.lunch: Final meal in Rome — return to your favorite restaurant from the week, or try one last new spot. Recommended: a final visit to Harvest Moon Café or Pastime Restaurant. Budget ~$12–15.
meals.dinner: Airport or travel meal depending on departure schedule. Budget ~$10–15.

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated daily food budget: ~$25–35/day using the grocery + selective dining strategy. Total 7-day food budget estimate: ~$175–245. Free and low-cost attractions kept activity costs minimal — most days under $15 in admission fees. Rome, GA is a genuinely charming small city with real art, history, and food culture worth exploring on a budget.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome (15 Chateau Drive). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented. Take a leisurely stroll around the immediate neighborhood to shake off travel fatigue and get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk – Join a guided evening walk through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere, sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, local wines, and other Roman street bites. A perfect low-effort, high-reward introduction to Rome's culinary soul after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: N/A – in transit (grab something at the airport if needed)
meals.dinner: Covered as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk – multiple tastings included. Supplement with a gelato from a local gelateria afterward.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given the 16:00 arrival. Pre-book the Trastevere evening walk in advance as it often sells out. Wear comfortable walking shoes. June evenings are warm (~22–24°C) so light layers are fine.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel – Start early (pre-booked skip-the-line entry for 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds and the midday heat. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the vast papal art collections, the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber and explore the Castel Sant'Angelo (Hadrian's Mausoleum) – a mid-range entry fee and stunning views from the top. Then stroll along the Via della Conciliazione and rest at a nearby café during the hottest part of the day (around 29–30°C).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Prati neighborhood (steps from the Vatican) for dinner – a lively, authentic Roman district popular with locals. Browse the evening passeggiata along Via Cola di Rienzo.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café – grab a cornetto and cappuccino at a local bar (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Pizzarium Bonci (Via della Meloria, Prati) – Rome's most celebrated pizza al taglio spot, mid-range and perfect for a quick, delicious lunch (€10–15)
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo (Prati) – a beloved neighborhood trattoria serving classic Roman pasta dishes like cacio e pepe and carbonara; set menu around €25–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance online. Dress code enforced – no bare shoulders or shorts above the knee inside the Vatican. Bring a water bottle; June heat can be intense by midday.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour – Book a timed-entry guided tour (mandatory, 2-hour slots) for the 9:00 AM session. Marvel at Bernini's extraordinary sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings in this intimate villa setting. One of Rome's most rewarding art experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, take a relaxing walk through the surrounding Villa Borghese gardens – Rome's green lung. Rent a rowboat on the lake or simply picnic in the shade. Then descend to the Spanish Steps and the Trevi Fountain area for classic sightseeing (best visited mid-afternoon when morning crowds thin slightly).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively streets around the Pantheon and Piazza Navona. Toss a coin at the Trevi Fountain at dusk for a magical atmosphere, then wander to dinner in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Café Sant'Eustachio or similar – espresso and pastry near the hotel before heading out (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens – pick up fresh bread, cheese, cured meats, and fruit from a nearby alimentari or deli (€10–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Ristorante da Francesco (Piazza del Fico, near Piazza Navona) – a reliable mid-range trattoria with excellent Roman classics and outdoor seating; €30–40 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets MUST be booked well in advance (often weeks ahead) – only 360 visitors allowed per 2-hour slot. The gallery is a 10-minute walk from the park entrance. Wear sunscreen and a hat for the afternoon garden walk.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk – Arrive early (9:00 AM opening) to explore the ancient heart of the Roman Empire before the heat peaks. Walk through the Forum where Julius Caesar was cremated, climb Palatine Hill for panoramic views over the ruins, and imagine emperors and senators at work. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: From the Forum, walk to the Colosseum (combo ticket covers Forum + Palatine Hill + Colosseum). Explore the iconic amphitheater, then cool off with a gelato on the nearby Via Sacra. Rest at a café during the hottest hours (2:00–4:00 PM). Later, explore the Circus Maximus and Aventine Hill, including the famous Knights of Malta keyhole view of St. Peter's dome.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Testaccio neighborhood – Rome's most authentic working-class district – for a relaxed evening of aperitivo and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bar San Calisto or a local café in Trastevere/Testaccio area – cornetto and cappuccino (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Forno Roscioli (Via dei Chiavari) or a nearby trattoria near the Forum – simple Roman lunch of suppli, pizza bianca, or a pasta dish (€12–18)
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) – a legendary Roman trattoria built into the Monte dei Cocci (ancient pottery shard hill), serving outstanding cacio e pepe and rigatoni alla pajata; €30–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buy combined Forum/Palatine/Colosseum tickets online in advance to avoid long queues. Saturday mornings can be busy – arrive right at opening. Comfortable, closed-toe shoes essential for uneven ancient cobblestones. Stay hydrated in the heat.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour – Dive into Rome's culinary soul at the Mercato Testaccio, the city's most authentic covered food market. Join a guided offal and street food tour to taste porchetta, supplì, fried artichokes, cured meats, aged cheeses, and the famous quinto quarto (fifth quarter) dishes that define Roman cuisine. A must for food lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, visit the nearby Pyramid of Cestius (a surprising ancient Egyptian-style tomb) and the Protestant Cemetery where Keats and Shelley are buried – a peaceful, shaded retreat. Then take a leisurely walk along the Tiber riverbank. If energy allows, visit the Mouth of Truth (Bocca della Verità) at Santa Maria in Cosmedin church.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere for a relaxed Sunday evening – Rome's most atmospheric neighborhood comes alive on Sunday nights with locals and visitors alike. Browse artisan shops and enjoy the golden-hour light on the medieval streets.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or a quick café stop before the market tour (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Tastings are included in the Testaccio Market Food Tour – this serves as a substantial late morning/early lunch experience
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 (Trastevere) – a beloved, intimate Roman trattoria with exceptional cacio e pepe and coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew); book ahead; €30–38 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market is open Tuesday–Sunday mornings (closes around 2:00 PM). Book the food tour in advance. Sunday in Rome means many churches are open for free – a great opportunity to peek inside Santa Maria in Trastevere. Afternoon pace is intentionally relaxed – a mid-trip rest day.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lesser-visited but stunning Capitoline Museums – the world's oldest public museums, perched on Capitoline Hill with incredible views over the Roman Forum. See the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, Caravaggio paintings, and ancient Roman sculptures. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Campo de' Fiori market (mornings only, but the square is lively all day) and then explore the Jewish Ghetto – one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhoods. Visit the Great Synagogue and Museum of Jewish Rome. Browse the narrow streets and artisan workshops. Stop at the Largo di Torre Argentina (where Julius Caesar was assassinated) – now open as an archaeological site.
day_by_day.evening: Final splurge evening: enjoy aperitivo hour (6:00–8:00 PM) at a rooftop bar with views over Rome's skyline, then a memorable farewell dinner in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the hotel (€4–7)
meals.lunch: Nonna Betta (Jewish Ghetto) – a celebrated kosher-style Roman-Jewish restaurant; try the carciofi alla giudia (deep-fried artichokes) and pasta dishes; €25–35 per person
meals.dinner: Il Sorpasso (Prati) or Osteria Barberini (near Trevi) – excellent mid-range Roman dining with seasonal ingredients and a good wine list; €35–45 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Capitoline Museums are closed on Mondays – check current schedule and substitute with Palazzo Altemps or Palazzo Massimo (National Roman Museum) if needed, both excellent alternatives with world-class ancient art. The Jewish Ghetto restaurants are closed on Saturdays (Shabbat) but open Monday.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome – revisit a favorite spot or explore something missed. Consider the Pantheon (free entry, opens 9:00 AM) – one of the best-preserved ancient buildings in the world and a masterpiece of Roman engineering. Spend time in the surrounding piazzas, do any last-minute souvenir shopping (look for quality items: leather goods, ceramics, local food products like pasta and olive oil).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: enjoy a long, leisurely final Roman lunch. Pack, check out of the hotel, and transfer to the airport or onward destination. If time allows, a final gelato stop is mandatory.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or onward travel.

meals.breakfast: A proper Roman bar breakfast – stand at the counter like a local for the authentic experience; espresso and cornetto (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Armando al Pantheon – a historic, beloved trattoria steps from the Pantheon serving traditional Roman cuisine since 1961; book ahead; €35–45 per person – a perfect farewell meal
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight, depending on departure schedule

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (typically 11:00 AM – ask about late checkout if your flight is in the evening). The Pantheon now requires a timed entry ticket (€5) – book online. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours for airport transfer and check-in. Rome's FCO airport is approximately 30–45 minutes from the city center by train (Leonardo Express) or 45–60 minutes by taxi.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: N/A – in transit / airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: Included tastings on the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk; supplement with a sit-down finale at Ristorante Paris (Trastevere) – a historic Roman trattoria with white-tablecloth elegance, known for cacio e pepe and coda alla vaccinara.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer. Keep Day 1 light given afternoon arrival and potential jet lag. Confirm Trastevere walk booking in advance as evening slots fill quickly in June.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel – Begin with an exclusive early-access or skip-the-line private guided tour of one of the world's greatest art collections. Spend 3–4 hours exploring the Raphael Rooms, Gallery of Maps, and culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Arrive by 8:00 AM to beat the crowds and the midday heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber to Castel Sant'Angelo for a self-guided exploration of its ramparts and panoramic river views. Then retreat to the hotel for a mid-afternoon rest during the hottest part of the day (peak ~30°C). Optional: visit a nearby luxury boutique or art gallery.
day_by_day.evening: Elegant dinner in the Prati neighborhood near the Vatican, renowned for upscale dining. Enjoy the cooler evening air with an aperitivo on a terrace before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at a classic Roman bar – cornetto and cappuccino at Caffè San Pietro near the Vatican.
meals.lunch: Il Sorpasso (Prati) – a stylish wine bar and bistro with an outstanding charcuterie selection, natural wines, and Roman small plates. Perfect post-Vatican refuel.
meals.dinner: Il Matriciano (Prati) – a beloved Roman institution serving traditional pasta dishes like amatriciana and carbonara in a refined yet authentic setting. Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums tickets well in advance – June is peak season. Consider a private guide for a richer experience. Wear comfortable shoes; the Vatican complex involves extensive walking on marble floors.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour – Visit this intimate world-class gallery housing Bernini's stunning sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic masterworks. Entry is strictly timed (2-hour slots); a private guide elevates the experience enormously. Book the 9:00 AM slot to enjoy the gallery at its quietest.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, stroll through the Villa Borghese gardens – Rome's most elegant park – for a relaxed walk among fountains and umbrella pines. Visit the Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping views over Piazza del Popolo and the Roman skyline. Descend to the Spanish Steps area for window shopping along Via Condotti (Bulgari, Valentino, Fendi).
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at a rooftop bar with views of the city, followed by a refined dinner in the Tridente district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Antico Caffè Greco (Via Condotti) – Rome's oldest café, open since 1760, beloved by Keats, Byron, and Goethe. Enjoy a leisurely espresso and pastry in gilded surroundings.
meals.lunch: Nino (Via Borgognona, Tridente) – a Florentine-Roman classic beloved by locals and discerning visitors; excellent bistecca and ribollita in a warm, wood-paneled room.
meals.dinner: La Pergola (Rome Cavalieri Hotel) – Rome's only three-Michelin-star restaurant, helmed by Chef Heinz Beck. An unmissable luxury dining experience with panoramic city views. Reserve weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery is strictly limited to 360 visitors per 2-hour session – advance booking is mandatory. La Pergola requires formal attire and reservations made well ahead of travel.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk – Take a private guided tour through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire. Walk where emperors lived on Palatine Hill, survey the ruins of temples and triumphal arches in the Forum below, and gain privileged insight into 2,000 years of history. Start at 8:30 AM before the heat and crowds intensify.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Capitoline Museums (Musei Capitolini) – the world's oldest public museums, housing the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and sweeping Forum views from the terrace. Then take a private car to the Aventine Hill for the Knights of Malta keyhole view of St. Peter's dome – a hidden Roman gem.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Testaccio neighborhood, Rome's authentic culinary heartland, just below Aventine Hill.

meals.breakfast: Roscioli Caffè Pasticceria (near Campo de' Fiori) – Rome's most celebrated bakery-café; extraordinary cornetti, maritozzi, and espresso. Worth the short drive.
meals.lunch: Terrazza Caffarelli (Capitoline Museums rooftop café) – enjoy a light lunch of Roman antipasti and wine with a spectacular panoramic view over the ancient city.
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) – a beloved institution built into the Monte Testaccio hill, serving impeccable Roman classics: rigatoni con pajata, cacio e pepe, and abbacchio. Rustic-chic atmosphere with premium wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Combined Forum/Palatine/Colosseum ticket available; consider adding Colosseum if energy allows. Wear sun protection – the Forum is fully exposed with minimal shade. June Saturdays are busy; private guide access helps navigate crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour – Dive deep into Rome's culinary soul at the Mercato Testaccio, the city's most authentic covered food market. A guided tour introduces you to vendors selling aged pecorino, cured guanciale, fresh pasta, and the famous quinto quarto (offal) dishes that define Roman cooking. Sample as you go with expert commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pyramid of Cestius and the Protestant Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico) – a hauntingly beautiful and little-visited gem where Keats and Shelley are buried, surrounded by ancient Roman walls. Then head to the Trastevere neighborhood for a leisurely afternoon exploring its medieval churches (Santa Maria in Trastevere) and artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the Janiculum Hill (Gianicolo) – Rome's best panoramic viewpoint – followed by dinner back in Trastevere.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before the market tour – save appetite for market tastings.
meals.lunch: Tastings at Testaccio Market constitute a substantial late-morning meal; supplement with a glass of Frascati white wine at a market wine bar.
meals.dinner: Glass Hostaria (Trastevere) – a Michelin-starred contemporary Roman restaurant with a sleek glass-and-steel design contrasting beautifully with the medieval surroundings. Chef Cristina Bowerman's creative Italian cuisine is exceptional.

day_by_day.notes: Testaccio Market is closed Sundays – reschedule this experience to a weekday if possible, or confirm current Sunday hours. If unavailable Sunday, substitute with a private cooking class at a Trastevere culinary studio instead.

day_by_day.morning: Private Art & Architecture Walking Tour of the Historic Center – Explore the Pantheon (arrive at opening, 9:00 AM, for an uncrowded experience), Piazza Navona with Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, and the hidden baroque churches of Sant'Ignazio and San Luigi dei Francesi (home to three Caravaggio masterpieces). A private art historian guide brings the layers of history alive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure afternoon for personal exploration or luxury shopping. Visit Campo de' Fiori's afternoon market atmosphere, browse the antique dealers along Via dei Coronari, or indulge in a spa treatment at the hotel. Alternatively, take a private car to the MAXXI (National Museum of 21st Century Arts) for a dose of contemporary Italian art in Zaha Hadid's landmark building.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve cocktails at a celebrated rooftop bar, followed by a grand dinner at one of Rome's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Sant'Eustachio il Caffè (near the Pantheon) – widely considered Rome's best espresso, served with their signature gran caffè. A Roman institution since 1938.
meals.lunch: Armando al Pantheon – a family-run Roman trattoria steps from the Pantheon, serving refined traditional Roman cuisine since 1961. Book ahead; it fills quickly even on weekdays.
meals.dinner: Il Pagliaccio (Via dei Banchi Vecchi) – a two-Michelin-star restaurant offering an exquisite tasting menu blending Japanese precision with Italian ingredients. One of Rome's most creative and intimate fine dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: The Pantheon now charges an entry fee (€5); book timed entry online. San Luigi dei Francesi Caravaggio chapel requires coins for the light machine – bring change. MAXXI is closed Mondays; confirm opening days before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure – enjoy a slow hotel breakfast, then take a private car for a last scenic drive past the Colosseum, Circus Maximus, and along the Appian Way for a glimpse of Rome's ancient outskirts. Stop at the Baths of Caracalla exterior for photographs. Alternatively, revisit a favorite neighborhood for last-minute souvenir shopping (artisan leather goods on Via della Croce, gourmet provisions at Roscioli Salumeria).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Depending on departure time, enjoy a final Roman lunch before private chauffeur transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure / in transit.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or a final visit to a beloved Roman café – consider returning to Sant'Eustachio or Antico Caffè Greco for a nostalgic send-off.
meals.lunch: Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio (near Piazza di Spagna) – a charming, upscale Roman trattoria perfect for a relaxed final lunch; excellent seafood antipasti and house-made pasta.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at departure airport lounge.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for afternoon activities. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport transfer and check-in. Purchase any gourmet provisions (aged pecorino, bottarga, artisan pasta) at Roscioli or Eataly Roma before departure – ideal luxury food souvenirs.

query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June from Chicago
